Force5

The design system behind wingfoil.ie's Force5 forecast map: a glass-on-sea surface language over one neutral ramp, one accent and one canonical wind scale.

v0.5.0 · schema 1 · 203 tokens (24 mode-varying) · 9 components · modes: light, dark

Components

Surface

Every floating thing in Force5 is a surface: a pane of tinted glass, blurred over the map, edged with a lit stroke so it reads as an object and not a stain. The map is the only thing in the product that is not on a surface.

Variants
5
States
2
  • .f5-surface — the default pane. Panels, popovers, the layers panel.
  • .f5-surface--pill — the same glass at pill radius, for floating chrome.
  • .f5-surface--dock — edge to edge along the bottom, square, casting upward.
  • .f5-surface--dialog — modal radius, dialog padding, above the scrim.
  • .f5-surface--sunken — a recess inside a surface. No blur, no shadow.

Button

Everything the user can press. Force5 has one filled action per view; everything else is quiet until it is touched.

Variants
6
States
4
  • .f5-button — quiet. The default, and the right answer nearly always.
  • .f5-button--primary — filled with --sem-color-action-bg. One per view.
  • .f5-button--pill — quiet, capsule, bordered. Floating chrome that must read as pressable against a moving map.
  • .f5-button--icon — a circle, no label, aria-label required.
  • .f5-button--link — underlined text, for a recovery action inside a sentence.
  • Sizes: .f5-button--sm (30px), default (40px), .f5-button--lg (46px).

Chip

A small read-only pill that states a fact: which model is running, how many spots matched, whether the pipeline is current. A chip is never pressable — if it can be pressed it is a .f5-button--pill.

Variants
4
States
3
  • .f5-chip — the default, on --sem-color-surface-raised.
  • .f5-chip--glass — free-floating over the map; carries its own glass and border.
  • .f5-chip--status — leads with a dot; data-status="ok|warn" colours it.
  • .f5-chip--warn — the whole chip in the warm family, for a degraded state.

Segmented control

A small set of mutually exclusive choices, all visible at once: knots or metres per second, which forecast model. Use it up to four options; past that it is a list, not a segmented control.

Variants
2
States
4
  • .f5-segmented — horizontal, the default.
  • .f5-segmented--stack — vertical, for a model list inside a popover.

Spot marker

What a location looks like on the map. The kind of place decides the shape, so the map is readable before any colour is understood: riding spots are round and carry a wind number, operators are squared, areas are dashed.

Variants
4
States
4
  • .f5-spot-marker — a riding spot. Round, shows knots.
  • .f5-spot-marker--operator — a school or hire centre. Squared at --sem-radius-control.
  • .f5-spot-marker--club — a club. Round, no reading.
  • .f5-spot-marker--area — a region rather than a point. Dashed border.

Wind scale

The legend for the one thing this product measures. It is the only component that may explain colour, because it is the only place the wind ramp is defined for the reader.

Variants
2
States
2
  • .f5-wind-scale — the default horizontal legend.
  • .f5-wind-scale--compact — shorter bar and fewer ticks, for narrow viewports.

Open the demo →

Forecast chart

The dock's uncertainty views: a probability blend and a candle column, plus the display filter that decides what the dock shows. This is the first component in the system that draws data rather than chrome, and the first one allowed to use a colour family outside the teal ramp — see the ruling of 2026-09-16. The chart never explains wind speed with a new palette. Height on the value axis _is_ speed, and the fill is the wind ramp read off that axis, so a band that reaches the yellow part of the scale is yellow for the same reason the map is.

Variants
3
States
14
  • .f5-forecast-chart--blend — the probability band. The default.
  • .f5-forecast-chart--candles — one candle per three-hour column: wick for the full range, body for the middle half, tick for the median, and a thin warm bar beside it for the gust range.
  • .f5-forecast-filter — the display filter, a solid raised surface. It is a dialog and not a second pane on purpose: the dock is already glass, and glass inside glass is mud.

Open the demo →

Site menu

The three lines. wingfoil.ie is two apps on one origin — the wind map and the second-hand gear marketplace — and this is the one control that says so and moves between them. It is chrome that floats over the map and sits in the marketplace header, so it is the same component in both, never two. It is a disclosure, not a menubar: a button that reveals a short <nav> of links. Every link is a real href, because the two sections are separate bundles chosen at load time and crossing between them is a page load.

Variants
2
States
7
  • .f5-site-menu — the only one of its own. Two sections is not a shape that needs variants: the menu always hangs from the left edge of its trigger, and the trigger always sits at the start of the chrome it belongs to, on both apps. A right-hung panel is the obvious next variant and is deliberately not here until something needs it.
  • The trigger takes the button's own sizes — .f5-button--sm beside a row of small pills, the default beside 40px chrome — because the menu has to sit in scale with whatever header it is in. Its height on a finger does not shrink with it; its width does, and padding that out is the parent's job, exactly as the system already requires of --sem-control-height-sm.
